symptom: LVS mismatch: missing, shorted, or open nets

first_checks.check: Extract the exact net name(s) and pin/device terminals flagged in the LVS error report and cross-reference against both schematic and layout connectivity viewers
first_checks.why_first: Immediately localizes the discrepancy to a handful of nets and rules out global extraction or deck failures

first_checks.check: Confirm the layout is DRC-clean on the metal/via layers involved and that no floating metal or unconnected via shapes exist on those nets
first_checks.why_first: Cheapest physical inspection that rules out the most common layout-editing oversights

first_checks.check: Re-run LVS with hierarchical comparison disabled (flat mode) on the failing block only
first_checks.why_first: Discriminates hierarchical black-box or interface mapping errors from true connectivity problems

discriminating_experiments.experiment: Temporarily short the suspect open net at the layout terminals (or cut the shorted path) with a zero-resistance ideal metal and re-extract; observe whether the LVS error count drops by exactly one
discriminating_experiments.rules_in: True geometric open or short in the drawn geometry

discriminating_experiments.experiment: Force a pure-text netlist comparison (ignore geometry) after renaming the schematic net to match the extracted name; check if the mismatch vanishes
discriminating_experiments.rules_out: Actual missing connectivity or unintended short

discriminating_experiments.experiment: Re-extract with via-enclosure and metal-overlap rules deliberately loosened by 10–20 %; see whether previously open nets now connect
discriminating_experiments.rules_out: Genuine missing via or metal break

common_root_causes.cause: Missing or under-sized via/contact that fails extraction connectivity rules
Unintended metal short caused by abutment or over-drawn polygon that extraction merges
Hierarchical port or pin-name mismatch between schematic symbol and layout abstract
Floating metal or unconnected device terminal left after ECO edits
Power/ground net short through an ESD or decap structure whose connectivity is only visible after full-chip extraction

classic_trap: Assuming every reported short is a real layout error and spending days searching polygons when the root cause is an extraction deck that merges adjacent nets under aggressive overlap rules
node_era_note: At 7 nm and below, via-resistance and multi-cut via extraction tolerances become far tighter, so many ‘opens’ that passed at 28 nm now fail unless the deck is re-tuned

symptom: LVS mismatch: wrong device sizes or extra devices

first_checks.check: Identify the exact device instance and parameter (W/L, m-factor, fingers) flagged in the LVS report and compare the schematic value against the extracted geometric measurement
first_checks.why_first: Localizes the mismatch to a single device type and immediately shows whether the error is size, multiplicity, or recognition

first_checks.check: Verify that the layout device recognition rules (layer combinations that define MOS, RES, CAP, etc.) match the PDK documentation for the technology
first_checks.why_first: Rules out the most frequent cause of phantom or missing devices before any geometry editing

first_checks.check: Confirm that the schematic netlist was generated with the correct process option and that no parasitic extraction was accidentally mixed into the LVS comparison
first_checks.why_first: Eliminates tool-flow or option-setting errors that produce systematic size or device-count deltas

discriminating_experiments.experiment: Force device recognition with a deliberately relaxed width/length tolerance (e.g., ±5 %) and re-run LVS; observe whether the size-mismatch errors disappear while device count stays constant
discriminating_experiments.rules_out: Wrong device type or extra parasitic device

discriminating_experiments.experiment: Selectively disable recognition of one device class (e.g., poly resistors or MOM capacitors) and re-extract; check whether the extra-device count drops by the expected number
discriminating_experiments.rules_in: False-positive recognition of a parasitic or intentional structure
discriminating_experiments.rules_out: True extra schematic device or missing layout instance

discriminating_experiments.experiment: Compare the extracted device count and total gate width against a pure schematic device audit (ignore geometry); if counts match but sizes differ, the problem is measurement, not recognition

common_root_causes.cause: Incorrect multiplicity or finger count drawn in layout versus the schematic m-factor
Device recognition rule that incorrectly identifies a parasitic structure (e.g., poly over diffusion) as an intentional MOSFET or resistor
Width/length measurement difference caused by drawn-versus-effective size or OPC bias not accounted for in the LVS deck
Extra devices introduced by an un-black-boxed IP block or by a fill structure that the recognition deck treats as active devices
Schematic generated with the wrong process corner or device model variant so that L and W defaults differ from layout

classic_trap: Editing the layout device geometry to ‘fix’ a size mismatch when the real problem is an LVS deck that reports drawn size instead of the electrical (post-bias) size expected by the schematic
node_era_note: At 7 nm and below, multi-patterning and cut-mask effects make effective W/L extraction far more sensitive to deck settings than at 28 nm, where drawn dimensions were usually sufficient
